text:
Alex: quick idea — what if we align per-org RPM/TPM caps to SLA tiers and add a short leaky-bucket probe to detect micro-spikes?
Maria: TL;DR: SLA tiers map -> different leak rates + different fast-fail thresholds? :thinking:
Kevin: I'm worried about adding more knobs. how would this interact with existing burst_window_seconds and grace credits?
Anya: Proposal: use probe requests (cheap, low-priority) to measure spike shape. if probe shows < 3s tail, allow a short fast-burst (fast-fail otherwise).
Alex: sketch of policy config (P0):
```yaml
policy_name: sla_aligned_v1
tier: gold
rpm: 12000
tpm: 60000
concurrency: 50
burst_window_seconds: 20
burst_allowance_tokens: 200
leaky_bucket_probe: true
probe_sample_rate: 0.01
probe_latency_threshold_ms: 3000
```
Maria: That probe_sample_rate looks low but should be sufficient to detect high-frequency spikes without noise. It'd live in the router before batching.
Kevin: how do we surface this in Console? need a dashboard card: "Short-burst activity" with 95/99% probe latency and a histogram of burst durations. otherwise SRE will be flooded.
Anya: also add a "fast-fail reason" tag on responses so telem can separate droppped-by-probe vs throttled-by-quota. e.g. X-Rate-Limit-Reason: probe_fastfail
Alex: UX: allow product teams to opt-in per-org to allow short bursts for 1 minute windows. default = opt-out for enterprise contracts.
Maria: implementation note: router should compute an "effective leak rate" = tier_base_leak * (1 + short_burst_multiplier) when probe signals smooth tail. makes smoothing deterministic.
Kevin: curious about billing: if we fast-fail, should we refund tokens? I propose marking requests as billed=false in usage pipeline when fast-fail==true. ops-bot: we need legal sign-off on that.
Anya: failure modes: probe misclassification during traffic ramps -> could falsely allow big bursts. mitigate via backoff: if any backend error rate rises > 0.5% after allow, retract for 5m.
Alex: minimal logs we need: probe_sample_id, probe_latency_ms, allowed_burst_tokens, decision(allow/reject), reason. sample log: `probe=1234 latency_ms=210 allow=1 tokens=40 reason=tail_ok`.
deploy-bot: routing change PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/p/rate-router/merge-214 (WIP)
Maria: Can someone add a ticket to Console backlog to show probe hist & "opt-in per-org" toggle? I'll own it if Kevin wires API.
Kevin: will add api flag: org.ratepolicy.allow_short_burst = boolean + org.ratepolicy.leak_multiplier. I'll open a tiny API PR.
Anya: sounds good. plan: 1) small probe server-side flag and logs 2) router decision + metric 3) console card + opt-in toggle 4) rollout to non-prod then canary.
Alex: thumbs up. let's avoid adding rate-structure complexity for free-tier until after we measure in canary. :thumbsup:
Maria: noted. will create the backlog ticket and add design screenshots.
Kevin: PR in ~2 days. tagging @Anya for canary run.
Anya: happy to run canary and monitor. I'll set alert: probe-allowed-drop-rate > 0.2% -> rollback.
Alex: thanks all — keeping this lightweight and observable is key.
